ios.desc:
Read real books in Spanish, French, German, Japanese and 25 more languages. Tap any word to see what it means in this exact sentence, save it as a flashcard, and keep reading. Free, no account, no ads.

LinguaRead is an EPUB reader built for language learners. Instead of a dictionary that lists ten meanings, you get the one that fits the sentence you are reading, including idioms, slang and figurative language.

READ REAL BOOKS
• Import any EPUB: classics, modern novels, textbooks
• Free public-domain classics from Project Gutenberg in 30 languages, right inside the app
• Curated starter picks for learners in Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese and more
• Clean, quiet reader with progress tracking and daily reading goals

TRANSLATIONS THAT FIT THE SENTENCE
• Tap a word: meaning in context, not a generic definition
• Tap the info button for a full explanation of grammar and usage
• Translate the whole sentence when you need more
• Hear the pronunciation of any word

FLASHCARDS WITH CONTEXT
• Every saved word keeps the sentence it came from
• Spaced repetition with adjustable intervals runs your daily review
• Streaks, goals and reminders keep you consistent
• Word notifications during the day, export your deck to CSV for Anki or Quizlet

WORKS EVERYWHERE
• iPhone, iPad, Mac and Apple Vision Pro
• iCloud sync of your library, progress and flashcards
• Only 19 MB, works offline for reading and review

PRIVACY FIRST
• No account, no tracking, no ads
• Your books and progress stay on your device or in your own iCloud
• Only the selected text is sent for translation, in real time, and never stored
• Bring your own OpenAI, Anthropic or Gemini API key if you prefer

PRICING
Free: unlimited reading, flashcards and study tools, plus 5 contextual translations per day.
Premium (optional): unlimited translations and early access to newer AI models. Monthly or yearly, cancel anytime.

Languages in the library: English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Russian, Ukrainian, Polish, Dutch, Swedish, Norwegian, Danish, Finnish, Czech, Hungarian, Romanian, Bulgarian, Greek, Turkish, Japanese, Chinese, Korean, Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, Hindi, Thai, Vietnamese, Indonesian.

Privacy Policy: https://yevgenii.dev/projects/linguaread/privacy
Terms of Use: https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/dev/stdeula/

show_hn.title: Show HN: An iOS reader that lets you translate words inline while reading

quotes.text:
I’ve been trying to read books in foreign languages for a long time, and the biggest problem for me was always the same:
every unknown word breaks the reading experience.

If I stop and open a dictionary, I lose the sentence and the rhythm.
If I ignore the word, I sometimes miss too much meaning.
Either way, reading turns into work instead of something enjoyable.

I ended up building a small iOS app for myself called LinguaRead. It opens EPUB books and lets you tap on a word to see what it means in the context of the sentence you’re reading. The goal isn’t perfect translation — it’s reducing friction enough to keep reading without constantly switching apps.

It’s a simple tool and still early, but it helped me read longer and finish more books in another language than I could before.

I’m curious how others here approach this problem:
Do you translate selectively or only when you’re stuck?
Do you mostly rely on context?
Do you reread books you already know in another language?

Happy to hear what’s worked (or not worked) for you, and open to feedback.
